notes:
Overview:
- Vertical: multi-tenant SaaS support platform serving mid-to-large enterprises. Primary product: agent-assist + customer self-serve widget.
- Data footprint: ~80M short documents (tickets, KB articles, replies). Index growth forecasted to 20% q/q.
- Peak load: estimated 120-180 qps across multi-tenant clusters; target safety capacity 250 qps.

Technical requirements / ask:
- Retrieval + rerank architecture to guarantee top-5 relevance precision for deflection flow. Ops insists on reranker in the critical path (cross-encoder preferred) for top-5 correctness.
- Latency SLO: 99th percentile end-to-end <250ms (hosted widget path). Soft target 95th <150ms for agent UI.
- Indexing scale: vectors for 80M docs, expect ~150-200M vectors with alternative chunking strategies. Need guidance on shard strategy and storage costs.
- Cost constraint: target amortized cost per query < $0.10 (including retrieval + rerank + model infer). Currently worried reranker costs push to $0.30/q.
- Model preferences: open to open-source cross-encoders (debiased small cross-encoders) and quantized transformer models; favor 8-bit quant for on-prem / Dedicated GPU footprint.
- Deployment: must run in customer VPC (private control plane acceptable). US-only residency and KMS integration mandatory.

POC findings so far (3/05 interim):
- Ingested 2M tickets: ANN retrieval latency ~70ms median (Faiss op), recall@100 OK.
- Cross-encoder (onnx, CPU-bound) rerank of top-50 -> top-10 averages 140ms single-thread; scaled CPU farm would increase cost linearly.
- Streaming candidate rerank + cache hot prefixes for repeated customer queries shows potential 2x cost savings.
- Batch rerank for deflection suggestions (precompute for common queries) discussed as a cost/latency tradeoff.

Stakeholder quotes / signals:
- “Top-5 answers must be correct enough that our widget's deflection rate improves without increasing false deflections.” — VP Product (L. Harrison).
- “If we can't hit 250ms 99th with predictable spend, we cannot route production traffic.” — Head of Ops (M. Rivera).

Decision factors they care about:
- Deterministic latency at 99th under sustained peak.
- Clear unit economics for rerank (per-query CPU/GPU cost) and advice on pre-rerank caching / batching.
- Security posture: SOC2 + SSO + KMS + US residency.

Proposed Redwood approach (SE notes):
- Dedicated GPU pool for latency-critical rerank; small quantized cross-encoder variant for rerank cost optimization.
- ANN storage split by tenant with sharding plan to keep hot-tenant working set resident.
- Use Redwood Optimize to recommend batch sizes, cache TTLs, and suggest quant & model combos by workload.
- Canary routing + automatic fallback to lighter reranker when Dedicated capacity constrained (preserves availability but degrades top-5 quality).

- Infra (Auringate) to provide 7-day peak logs and query distribution by 2026-03-09.
